accepted.s: With reference to oil palm cultivation in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following is correct for 2023–24?
o: 2.27 lakh ha area, 3.10 lakh farmers and 17.63 lakh MT crude palm oil production
1.74 lakh ha area, 2.27 lakh farmers and 3.10 lakh MT FFB production
2.27 lakh ha area, 1.74 lakh farmers and 17.63 lakh MT FFB production
1.74 lakh ha area, 17.63 lakh farmers and 2.27 lakh MT FFB production
accepted.x: In 2023–24, Andhra Pradesh led India in oil palm area and production, with 2.27 lakh ha, 1.74 lakh farmers and 17.63 lakh MT of fresh fruit bunches (FFB).
accepted.tq: Match the numerical figures with the correct crop and production indicators.
accepted.sec: Oil palm in AP - area, production, NMEO-OP

accepted.s: In 2023–24, Andhra Pradesh produced approximately how much crude palm oil?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh produced 3.10 lakh MT of crude palm oil in 2023–24.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the crude palm oil figure from the FFB production figure.
accepted.sec: Oil palm in AP - area, production, NMEO-OP

accepted.s: The earlier figure of oil palm production in Andhra Pradesh that was asked in an APPSC examination for 2017–18 was:
accepted.x: The earlier APPSC-asked figure for Andhra Pradesh oil palm production in 2017–18 was 17.81 lakh tonnes.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between close production figures belonging to different years.
accepted.sec: Oil palm in AP - area, production, NMEO-OP

accepted.s: How many acres were added to oil palm cultivation in Andhra Pradesh during 2024–25?
accepted.x: A further 39,502 acres were added to oil palm cultivation in Andhra Pradesh during 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Use year-wise numerical discrimination.
accepted.sec: Oil palm in AP - area, production, NMEO-OP

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding oil palm expansion in Andhra Pradesh during 2025–26:

accepted.x: All four statements are correct for the 2025–26 oil palm expansion programme in Andhra Pradesh.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following initiatives in chronological order:
A. National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm
B. Oilseeds Technology Mission
C. National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm
Select the correct sequence.

accepted.tq: Use the first-and-last years to establish the sequence.
accepted.sec: Oil palm in AP - area, production, NMEO-OP

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a target of NMEO-OP for 2025–26?
o: Adding 6.5 lakh ha and reaching 10 lakh ha of total area
Adding 10 lakh ha and producing 6.5 lakh tonnes of CPO
accepted.x: NMEO-OP seeks to add 6.5 lakh ha and reach 10 lakh ha of oil palm area by 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Separate area-expansion targets from production targets.
accepted.sec: Oil palm in AP - area, production, NMEO-OP

accepted.s: The crude palm oil production targets under NMEO-OP are correctly matched as:

11.20 lakh tonnes by 2025–26 and 28 lakh tonnes by 2029–30

accepted.s: India’s edible-oil import dependence declined from 63.2% in 2015–16 to what level in 2023–24?
accepted.x: Edible-oil import dependence fell to 56.25% in 2023–24 from 63.2% in 2015–16.
accepted.tq: Read the direction and exact endpoints of the trend.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the MIDH funding pattern?
o: 100% central funding for all States and institutions
60:40 for general States, 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and 100% central funding for NHB, CDB and CIH
50:50 for all States and 100% State funding for NHB, CDB and CIH
90:10 for general States, 60:40 for North-Eastern States, and 50% central funding for NHB
accepted.x: MIDH follows a 60:40 pattern in general States, 90:10 in North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and provides 100% central funding for NHB, CDB and CIH.
accepted.tq: Compare funding ratios by State category and institution.
accepted.sec: Schemes - MIDH, Cluster Development Programme

accepted.s:
Which of the following are sub-schemes of MIDH?
1. National Horticulture Mission
2. Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan States
3. National Oilseeds Mission
4. National Food Security Mission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The National Horticulture Mission and the Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan States are sub-schemes of MIDH.
accepted.tq: Identify the schemes that belong to the same horticulture framework.
accepted.sec: Schemes - MIDH, Cluster Development Programme

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT covered among the crop categories under MIDH?
accepted.x: MIDH covers horticultural crops including fruits and bamboo; it does not cover all cereal crops without exception.

accepted.s: RKVY support for horticulture in non-MIDH districts of Andhra Pradesh amounted to approximately how much in 2024–25?

accepted.sec: Schemes - MIDH, Cluster Development Programme

accepted.s: The National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP) is correctly described by which of the following?
o: It is a 100% centrally funded programme launched in September 2019 to eradicate FMD by 2030.
It is a 75% subsidised programme launched in 2014 to insure livestock.
It is a centrally sponsored programme launched in 2025 to promote feed plants.
